**Yes, but only some models, and it's not a perfect substitute for a real UPS.** A power station is a UPS only if it has documented UPS/EPS mode with automatic switchover. Otherwise it can drop your computer during an outage.

**What to check**
- **Switchover time:** Anker says a unit needs "documented UPS or EPS functionality, automatic switchover, a suitable transfer time" ([Anker](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)). EcoFlow warns that many products advertise UPS but switch in 30 ms or more, which can risk data corruption ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)). Both are manufacturers with products to sell, so treat the strong warnings with that in mind.
- **Not 0 ms:** Even 10-20 ms isn't zero. Anker says to check your device's manual, and if it requires 0 ms transfer, use an online double-conversion UPS instead ([Anker](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas)). For a typical desktop, a ≤10 ms unit is generally the safer bet, but I can't confirm your PSU's tolerance from these results.
- **Pure sine wave output** is preferable for computers and networking gear.
- **Pass-through and 24/7 use:** Confirm the model supports staying plugged in continuously, and use the specific outlet the manual designates for UPS mode.
- **Power and runtime:** Add up your computer's real wattage (a plug-in watt meter helps). Runtime ≈ Wh × ~0.85 ÷ load in watts.
- **Automatic shutdown:** Basic UPS mode keeps power on but may not signal your PC to shut down. EcoFlow lists UPS-HID support for some models, so check this if you want automatic shutdown.

**Options from the search results**
- **EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus** is the budget pick: <10 ms switchover and 600 W AC output, which EcoFlow says is plenty for a desktop and external drives. Details are in [EcoFlow's UPS article](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply). I didn't get a direct purchase page for it.
- **Anker SOLIX S2000** has a 10 ms UPS switchover, 2,010 Wh, and 1,500 W pure sine wave output. It was listed at $699.99 after coupon, and you can [see it on Anker's page](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups).
- **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2** has a ≤15 ms switchover, 2,074 Wh, and 2,600 W output. It's $899, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF. This is more capacity than most desktops need, and its 15 ms is the slowest of the three. [Buy at BLUETTI](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2). This is an affiliate link, so the seller pays a commission at no cost to you.

**Bottom line:** For a desktop or laptop where you want long runtime, a UPS-rated model with ≤10 ms switchover is reasonable. For a NAS, server, or anything where data loss is costly, a conventional online UPS is the safer choice. If you tell me your computer's wattage and whether you have a NAS, I can narrow this down.
